sections.overview: Pantala hymenaea is a strong-flying skimmer dragonfly native to the Americas and often associated with temporary pools.
sections.identification: A dark spot at each hindwing base distinguishes it from the similar Wandering Glider, Pantala flavescens; the face may turn red as adults mature.
sections.habitat: It uses temporary natural or artificial pools and may fly far from water over open ground, roads or towns.
sections.diet: Like other dragonflies it catches flying insects, but the species-specific sources consulted do not detail its prey.
sections.behavior: It is a powerful flier; an observer in Mexico recorded it as the most numerous dragonfly in a post-storm flight.
sections.reproduction: It is an early colonizer of temporary pools where it breeds, but sources do not establish one breeding season across its range.
sections.ecology: Its close relative P. flavescens is much more widely distributed; this species is limited to the New World but also disperses widely.
sections.conservation: The sources establish a broad range but not a current global population trend, so no global conservation status is inferred here.
